Unpack the top-line drivers behind the accelerating, significant growth (IRI showed up 144% in latest four weeks) and the US measured-retail piece.

Momentum from three megatrends, the PepsiCo partnership lifting ACV from ~60% to over 95%, strong unit growth signaling new consumers, expanded distribution, and ~44% new-to-category per Mintel - all evidence the strategy is working.
About the brand's differentiation (packaging, flavor profiles), how new-to-category share has evolved, and where those consumers come from.

The portfolio is 'really inviting' vs traditional energy; many consumers don't consider themselves energy drink consumers and pair it with lunch - a large foodservice opportunity. Cited the >2,000 Jersey Mike's launch, the over-18 Amazon share, the club business, and innovative flavors (Cosmic Vibe, Oasis Vibe/Prickly Pear Lime, Green Apple Cherry). Consumers loyal to Celsius but move between flavors.
Distribution durability beyond the PepsiCo lift

It could be tempting to think the growth ends at the Oct 1 PepsiCo anniversary, but distribution points are up ~4%/month since January - how does distribution grow within existing stores (secondary placements, facings).

Hitting 95% ACV does not end the game - Celsius averages ~14.6 SKUs/location vs ~25-30 for the top two who also multi-face, leaving huge runway for placement, more SKUs, multi-facing. Core/Vibe bifurcation targets 1-3 shelves each. 95% ACV just means 'in the door'; goal now is to 'get out of the gutter.' Entering NACS/convenience review season in October at a ~10 share trajectory (vs 3.4 a year ago) changes prioritization.
Have reset conversations started, is it a continuous process, and does momentum mean another wave of gains a year out ('lather, rinse, repeat').

Confirmed a continuous cycle. A Walmart pre-meeting went extremely well, plus an exploratory California meeting with Walmart leadership - as a former three-share brand Celsius was never invited to such meetings. Walmart is the biggest energy seller and Celsius is under-indexed there. Elaborated Core/Vibe: Vibe experiential with unique combinations, Core fruit-forward targeting the most refreshing energy drink, each with distinct marketing.
What is Celsius's Amazon share, has it been impacted by broader distribution, and what is the Amazon consumer like.

Just under a 19 share on Amazon, a couple percent below Monster, well ahead of Red Bull. Q2 showed over 100% growth in all channels - no cannibalization. Amazon consumer is a loyal repeat purchaser comfortable with a warm 18-pack, distinct from the C&G impulse buyer and Costco consumer; 'the tides are rising.' Celsius is #1 energy drink on Instacart.
What is the market share ceiling given no brand besides Red Bull/Monster has sustained above 10%, and how is Celsius positioned in South Florida.

Potential framed between the Amazon share (every brand treated equally) and the ~3-share national level. South Florida share rose from 21.7% (April) to 23.5% (Aug 13) - about two share points; it is a transient market and now 'in our backyard,' so the next call will cite other markets (e.g., unmarketed Buffalo, NY). A proof point that the brand performs well as the category evolves to 'energy 2.0.'
How foodservice expansion works with the PepsiCo partnership - whether Celsius and Pepsi jointly approach customers and what wins are on the horizon.

Celsius hired a retired Pepsi foodservice executive; expansion is largely joint partnerships leveraging Pepsi's connections and population reach (it would not be profitable to independently source ~2,000 restaurants). Opportunity includes Marriott, Hyatt, Sheraton, colleges (Pepsi reaches ~60% of college population), and Lowe's. Delivery thesis: few food-delivery orders include a beverage and many fast-casual consumers skip the fountain - Celsius could be incremental to the basket.
How management thinks about the international opportunity and what is next there.

Same global megatrends; already in Sweden (10+ share), growing Finland, with distribution/seeding in South Korea, Taiwan, Hong Kong, a China licensing agreement, Malaysia, and Philippines. 2023 a planning year connecting with PepsiCo Europe/APAC teams; some 2024 launches but the larger opportunity is 2025-2026 (2024 builds the blueprint). US has massive runway (~$310M US sales last quarter, ~100% growth) so the team stays US-focused; a market gets ~six months to perform at retail.
Beyond the Core/Vibe differentiation, what other innovation is in the works and how to build the portfolio without getting distracted from the core.

A cross-functional team meets monthly to evaluate innovation; focus on the core portfolio is most important now. Three-to-ten-year vision of Celsius as a versatile Gatorade-like brand able to play in functional waters and hydration. The largely unmarketed On-The-Go Stick powder business is already over $100M and growing rapidly (sold at Walmart, Target, Kroger) - an expansion opportunity within hydration.
What is the sustainable margin profile / long-term EBITDA outlook.

Did not commit to a specific sustainable EBITDA range; cited Monster's historical margins as the 'gold standard' aspiration (currently dented by industry-wide supply chain hiccups). With 100% growth, management is focused on investing behind growth and deliberately giving up some near-term margin - profitable growth, reinvesting earnings. Sees opportunities to slowly leverage gross margin and put S&M dollars to better use; lots of operating leverage in G&A and S&M as the business scales and improved shelf placement makes each dollar more effective.
